T-3041: the first fort's powder magazine gets its barrel vault (#1698)

Replace the first Fort Dearborn magazine's reconstructed gable with the vault
form the owner adopted on 2026-11-03 (T-3335/T-3041), comparing the Currey 1912
bird's-eye building by building against Whistler's measured plan.

Both pictures were read directly for this change, by their pinned hashes.
Whistler's draught of January 25, 1808 draws the magazine -- his index no. 4 --
in elevation with an arched front springing from its side walls. Currey's
bird's-eye at p. 27 of The Story of Old Fort Dearborn (1912) labels the same
building 8 and draws it under a rounded vault. The record's roof_type moves from
gable/reconstructed to barrel_vault/inferred, cited to both.

THE SHAPE IS ADOPTED; THE CURVE'S DEPTH IS NOT MATCHED. Neither picture gives a
radius, a rise, a thickness, a colour, a roofing fabric or a completion date, and
none was invented to supply one. The explicit reconstructed barrel_rise_m of
1.0286254881847008 m is envelope conservation: half the shorter unchanged 3.05 m
plan span times tan(34 deg), which holds the crown at 3.628625488184701 m, exactly
where the old gable's peak stood. That makes a shallow circular segment of radius
2.9860699863584146 m, where Whistler draws something near a semicircle; the gap
is stated, not closed. The obsolete roof_pitch_deg leaves the record, because a
curved roof has a varying tangent and one pitch figure would state something the
mesh does not contain. The old 34 degrees survives only inside the derivation.

The one edge that moves is the side eave: the same circle run out to the existing
0.30 m projection sits at 2.188061556 m rather than the gable's 2.397647445 m,
0.209586 m lower. Footprint, surveyed seat, bearing, phase dates, 4.51 m front,
3.05 m depth, 2.6 m wall, brick material, openings, covering and colour are all
unchanged, and nothing here is carried to the second fort's magazine.

The archetype grew an opt-in barrel_vault branch with a closed covering --
underside, front and rear fascia, two outer side eaves, no internal ribs and one
continuous height tone -- and brick end infills wound outward above the unchanged
rectangular walls. The parameter check REFUSES an invalid rise, a non-finite
derived radius, and a vault asked for with a chimney, gallery, cupola, lantern,
loopholes, a second storey or on any kind but a magazine, rather than clamping.

NATIVE REBUILD. The producer reaches 25 fort_structure defaults and 0 variants.
All 25 were genuinely rebuilt before this commit on pinned, sha256-verified
Blender 4.5.3 under Ubuntu 26.04, and the web derivatives re-encoded from that
build. Exactly one master moved a byte -- this magazine's -- and the other 24 came
back byte-identical, the second fort's magazine and the cupola blockhouse among
them. Every fort asset's inputs_sha256 changes, because the archetype's source is
part of a mesh's inputs; those are real freshness hashes from a real build. All
243 outbuilding masters, their derivatives and registry rows, and the T-3041
north-east pyramid, are untouched.

The before/after is a real same-camera render through the existing fourteen-member
Currey group camera from the committed GLBs; a pixel comparison of the two renders
changes only this building, and the previous render is kept beside the new one.
The magazine difference is marked fixed on the match record. The verdict stays
differs: the blockhouse cupolas and the western gateway are still open, and the
full first-fort acceptance is untouched. T-3041 and parent T-2387 stay open.
